newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh parliament to move to new capital by Oct 1.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh parliament to move to new capital by Oct 1.

text.p: Kazakhstan's parliament will move to the remote town of Akmola, designated by the president as the country's new capital, by October 1, a top parliamentarian said on Thursday.

"Of course, I am worried that not all the deputies will wish to move, and there may appear problems with the validity of their credentials," Marat Ospanov, chairman of Mazhilis, one of the two parliamentary houses, told a news conference.
But Ospanov said the deputies "should move to the new capital because the legislature must have the necessary quorum".
Akmola is a windswept town of about 300,000 people in a vast steppe land nearly 1,000 km (625 miles) west of the old capital Almaty.

Moving the state apparatus to Akmola, championed by President Nursultan Nazarbayev and approved by parliament, was ordered to be completed by the year 2000. But most banks, financial companies and some state economic bodies are expected to stay in Almaty.
The ministries of agriculture and transport and communications have already moved to the new capital, and Nazarbayev publicly promised he would be in Akmola on January 1 to welcome the new year.

Experts said the state elite was preparing to leave the old capital because of its disadvantageous geopolitical position on the south-eastern edge of Kazakhstan near the borders of China and Kyrgyzstan.

Almaty lies in the foothills of the geologically young Tien Shan mountains, where scientists forecast a strong earthquake in the coming years. Widespread environmental pollution in the heavily industrialised town (pop. 1.5 million) was another factor favouring relocation, officials said.
